# Upgrading from 0.1

Carve 0.2 is a source break, and it is still a development version. A 0.1 document can parse in 0.2 without an error and still render different HTML, so anyone who keeps 0.1 files has to act: authors run `carve upgrade` on each file, and hosts review their render options and stored trees. The tool rewrites what has one safe 0.2 spelling, checks each rewrite against the 0.1 HTML, and reports the rest for a person to review.

The largest changes:

- A block marker directly under a paragraph line no longer starts a block; insert a blank line ([paragraphs](./upgrade-0-2/paragraphs)).
- `---` and `___` breaks, `~~~` fences, `+` continuation lines, bare `_`, `~` and `=` pairs, and GFM separator rows lose their 0.1 meanings ([breaks](./upgrade-0-2/breaks), [lists](./upgrade-0-2/lists), [inline marks](./upgrade-0-2/inline), [tables](./upgrade-0-2/tables)).
- Raw HTML is escaped unless the host turns on `rawHtml` ([raw HTML](./upgrade-0-2/html)).
- Stored trees move to AST 2.0 ([AST](./upgrade-0-2/ast)).

## Run the rewrite tool {#tool}

Start with a copy of each 0.1 `.crv` file. Build `carve-js` on `main` with `npm ci` and `npm run build`. Its CLI is `node dist/cli.js` (installed as `carve`). In a working copy of a 0.1 document:

```sh
node dist/cli.js upgrade --check page.crv
node dist/cli.js upgrade --json page.crv
node dist/cli.js upgrade --write page.crv
node dist/cli.js fmt --write page.crv
```

`--check` writes nothing and exits 1 when a change or human review is needed. `--json` writes a structured report. Without `--write`, upgraded source goes to standard output and the report to standard error. `--write` replaces the input after checking the old and proposed HTML. A usage error exits 2. `--force` does not bypass an HTML mismatch. Run the tool **once per 0.1 file**: it is not idempotent on already upgraded source. This `upgrade` command is specific to the JavaScript reference engine; the shared 0.2 tooling contract does not require it.

Read the `rewrite`, `escape`, `report`, `upgrade-conflict` and `upgrade-mismatch` records. A mismatch prevents writing. Even a passing rewrite needs review: the tool's HTML comparison normalizes attribute order, whitespace between tags, and a leading line feed in list item text. Then compare representative pages rendered by both engines: headings and generated ids, list tightness and task items, table headers, footnotes, links, captions and raw HTML. The 0.2 output contract is HTML. Markdown, plain text and ANSI output come from export renderers (`carve render --to markdown`, `--to plain`, `--to ansi`); their output is engine behavior, not part of the specification (C2-T-003). Keep the JSON upgrade report with the source change for review.

## Reading this page {#reading}

Each area page opens with what 0.2 changed for one construct and why, then lists every row of the upgrade map for that construct by its row id. The upgrade guide holds the detail of each row and stays the normative record; each page closes with links to the guide sections that hold its rows.

- The left block is the 0.1 source. The right block is the 0.2 source the tool writes, as `carve fmt` writes it in turn (`crv`). Where the tool proposes no source, the right block shows what 0.2 makes of the unchanged 0.1 source (`html`, or a description in `text`).
- <Badge type="tip" text="rewrite" /> the tool changes the spelling. <Badge type="warning" text="escape" /> it escapes text that 0.2 would read as syntax. <Badge type="danger" text="report" /> a person has to decide. <Badge type="info" text="none" /> no source edit is needed.
- <Badge type="warning" text="silent" /> the unchanged 0.1 source still parses in 0.2 but renders different HTML. Review these rows even when a document has no syntax error.
- An invisible character in a sample, such as a tab-like control character or a no-break space, is shown as its code point, for example `⟨U+00A0⟩`. A tab is a real tab.

## Changes by area {#areas}

| Area | What changed |
|---|---|
| [Paragraphs and continuation](./upgrade-0-2/paragraphs) | A paragraph takes the next nonblank line, so a block marker under a paragraph line needs a blank line before it. |
| [Headings](./upgrade-0-2/headings) | `#` headings read as before; `=` headings are new, and tabs, comments and line endings in a heading line changed. |
| [Thematic breaks and typography](./upgrade-0-2/breaks) | `***` is the only thematic break; hyphen runs follow the dash rule, and smart quotes follow one opening rule. |
| [Lists and task items](./upgrade-0-2/lists) | Blank lines and content columns shape lists: `+` continuation lines and `{loose}` are gone. |
| [Description lists](./upgrade-0-2/descriptions) | Terms and descriptions own lines by column; an unindented line after a term ends it. |
| [Tables and captions](./upgrade-0-2/tables) | Header cells start with `\|=` and carry their alignment; the GFM separator row is gone. |
| [Emphasis and inline marks](./upgrade-0-2/inline) | Only `/` and `*` pair bare; underline, strike and highlight need the braced forms. |
| [Escapes](./upgrade-0-2/escapes) | Text that 0.2 would read as syntax is escaped to keep the 0.1 output. |
| [Code, math and fences](./upgrade-0-2/code) | A code or math span needs its closer, and backticks are the only code fence. |
| [Quotes, divs and admonitions](./upgrade-0-2/containers) | Quotes, divs and line blocks follow the top-level paragraph and column rules. |
| [Attributes](./upgrade-0-2/attributes) | Attribute lines apply to the next block only, and attribute text 0.1 dropped stays visible. |
| [Links, references and definitions](./upgrade-0-2/links) | Definitions stand at column 0, the first duplicate wins, and reference labels may wrap. |
| [Footnotes](./upgrade-0-2/footnotes) | A footnote body owns only its indented continuation. |
| [Comments](./upgrade-0-2/comments) | A `%%` comment runs to the end of its line; comment fences and frames changed. |
| [Metadata and frontmatter](./upgrade-0-2/metadata) | Line-1 frontmatter reads as before; typed metadata blocks are new. |
| [Includes](./upgrade-0-2/includes) | An include directive is a block of its own, with no inline include. |
| [Raw HTML and render options](./upgrade-0-2/html) | Raw HTML is escaped unless the host turns on `rawHtml`. |
| [Extensions and tabs](./upgrade-0-2/extensions) | Extensions get explicit source forms, and tab groups claim only blocks that are all tabs. |
| [Engine APIs](./upgrade-0-2/api) | The JavaScript, PHP and Rust calls that replace the 0.1 engine APIs. |
| [Command line and lint](./upgrade-0-2/cli) | The shared 0.2 commands, the flags that moved, and the new lint exit status. |
| [The AST 2.0 tree](./upgrade-0-2/ast) | Stored trees move to AST 2.0; every tree and field change. |
| [Withdrawn rows](./upgrade-0-2/withdrawn) | Row ids withdrawn after their ruling, mostly because 0.1 and 0.2 give the same HTML. |

**Specification (external):** [0.2 tooling contract](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/main/spec/0.2/tooling.md#scope); [HTML](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/main/spec/0.2/html.md); [upgrade map](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/main/spec/0.2/data/upgrade-map.json); [upgrade guide](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/main/spec/0.2/UPGRADING.md).
